content_metadata.description: An informative video explaining the CRISPR technology, its mechanism, and applications.

qAndA.answer: Guide RNA and Cas9 nuclease. (shown visually in Scene 3)
qAndA.question: What are the two components of the CRISPR system?

qAndA.answer: They cleave the target DNA sequence. (visually depicted in Scene 3)
qAndA.question: What is the function of the active sites in Cas9?

qAndA.answer: By recognizing and cleaving foreign DNA from phages, preventing them from replicating within the bacteria.
qAndA.question: How does CRISPR provide acquired immunity to bacteria?

qAndA.answer: Artificial immunization of bacteria used in food production and large-scale fermentation. (Scene 4)
qAndA.question: Besides genome editing, what is another application of CRISPR technology?

qAndA.answer: By comparing the spacer sequences within the CRISPR loci of different strains. (Scene 4)
qAndA.question: How can CRISPR be used to differentiate bacterial strains?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hey what's up everyone welcome to my YouTube channel LifeSense with KMD.
Today I'm going to explain about CRISPR which is also called as cluster regularly interspaced
short palindromic repeats.
Here the DNA loci contains short repetition of base sequence.
Reputation is followed by short segment of spacer DNA.
CRISPR loci range in size from 24 to 48 base pair.
Spacer DNA or region on for region of non coding DNA between tandemly repeated genes.
CRISPRs are found in approximately 40% of sequenced bacterial genome and 90% of sequenced
archaea.
CRISPR case system in prokaryotic is a prokaryotic humane system.
That means the CRISPR case system is a prokaryotic immune system.
Confer resistance to foreign genetic elements such as plasma, phage and provide a form
of acquired immunity.
CRISPR spacer recognize and cut these exogenous genetic elements.
Since 2013 the CRISPR case system has been used for gene editing and gene regulation.
Usually the CRISPR system consists of a two part.
One is a guide RNA which is a single stranded RNA which has a target specific CRISPR RNA sequence.
Another one is a case 9 nucleus which is a nucleus with a two active site.
So to form a CRISPR system these two will combine where one of the active site of the
nucleus CRISPR 9 will be bound with a target specific CRISPR RNA sequence.
Whenever the bacteria is infected with the bacterial phage, the bacterial phage will inject
its DNA inside the bacterial cell.
Once this DNA of the phage enter into the bacterial cell, this bacterial DNA will be taken by this
CRISPR system and that DNA will be complementary to the target specific CRISPR RNA sequence.
So when it will bind with that phage DNA, one of the active site will start to cleave,
both active sites start to cleave the target or the pathogen DNA.
That means the phage DNA will be cleaved by this nucleus activity of caspase 9.
So in this way the bacteria will be protected from the bacterial phage through CRISPR action.
Application Artificial immunization agonist phage by introduction of engineered CRISPR
loci in industrial, important bacteria including those used in food production and large scale
fermentation.
Genome engineering at cellular or organic level by programming reprogramming of CRISPR
cas system in system to achieve RNA guided genome engineering.
Discrimination of bacterial strain by comparison of spacer sequence.
Even it could be utilized for genome editing.
